DECISION 
On May 14, 2026, the Public Utilities Regulatory (Authority) reopened this 
proceeding pursuant to General Statutes § 16-9 for the limited purpose of adjudicating 
the Connecticut Natural Gas Corporation’s (CNG), The United Illuminating Company’s 
(UI), and The Southern Connecticut Gas Company’s (SCG; collectively, Avangrid) motion 
to modify Orders 1 and 2 of the March 3, 1987 Final Decision (Decision) in the above-
referenced proceeding (Motion No. 14). 
The Authority subsequently announced that it would hold a public hearing on June 
5, 2026, if requested in writing by 4:00 p.m. on May 21, 2026, for the purpose of 
discussing Avangrid’s request to modify the Orders. Notice of Hearing, May 14, 2026. 
Although the Office of Consumer Counsel (OCC) filed an objection to Motion No. 14, no 
party or intervenor requested a hearing; therefore, the Authority cancelled the hearing. 
Notice of Cancellation of Hearing, May 28, 2026. 
On May 19, 2026, the Connecticut Light and Power Company d/b/a Eversource 
Energy, Yankee Gas Services Company d/b/a Eversource Energy (collectively, 
Eversource; Eversource, with Avangrid, the Companies), and the Aquarion Water 
Company of Connecticut (Aquarion)1 filed a motion (Motion No. 15) seeking the same 
relief as Avangrid. The Authority broadened the scope of the reopened proceeding to 
also adjudicate Eversource’s request. Motion No. 15 Ruling, June 4, 2026, p. 2. 
The Authority subsequently announced that it would hold a public hearing on June 
17, 2026, if requested in writing by 4:00 p.m. on June 11, 2026, for the purpose of 
discussing Eversource’s request to modify the Orders. Notice of Hearing, June 4, 2026. 
Although OCC filed an objection to Motion No. 15,2 no party or intervenor requested a 
hearing; therefore, the Authority cancelled the hearing. Notice of Cancellation of Hearing, 
June 15, 2026. 
Order No. 1 of the Decision requires the Companies to submit their respective 10Q, 
10K, 8K, Quarterly Report, and Annual Report to the Authority no later than 10 days after 
filing them with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). Order No. 2 requires 
the Companies to file the following financial information on a quarterly basis: 

1 On June 30, 2026, Aquarion became a subsidiary of the Aquarion Water Authority in accordance with the 
transaction approved in Docket No. 25-04-03, Joint Application of Aquarion Water Authority, South 
Central Connecticut Regional Water Authority and Eversource Energy for Approval of a Change of 
Control. The Authority’s jurisdiction over Aquarion and AWA terminated at closing; therefore, Orders 
Nos. 1 and 2 are no longer applicable to Aquarion in this proceeding. See PURA Corresp. July 1, 2025, 
Docket No. 25-12-12, Application of Aquarion Water Company of Connecticut to Amend its Rate 
Schedules. 
2 OCC’s objections to Motion No. 14 and 15 were identical and were both filed on May 21, 2026. For ease 
of discussion, both objections will be referred to as the OCC Objection.

A) times pretax interest coverage (inclusive of Allowance for Funds Used During 
Construction (AFUDC) and deferred return when applicable); 
B) times pretax interest coverage and other non-cash accruals (excluding AFUDC 
an deferred return, where applicable); 
C) indenture coverage; 
D) net cash flow/ total permanent capital percentage; 
E) net cash flow/ cash construction percentage; 
F) return on common equity (both cost of capital method and next income method, 
both 12-month ending); 
G) AFUDC as a percentage of earnings and deferred return, where applicable; 
H) rate base; 
I) return on rate base; 
J) market to book, both dollars and ratio; 
K) dividends per share for the current quarter and 12 months ending; 
L) earnings per share for the current quarter and 12 months ending; 
M) capital structure: dollars and ratio and weighted cost of capital, including and 
excluding short-term debt; 
N) inflation rate (both the consumer price index and producers price index); and 
O) short-term interest rate to company and current prime rate. 
The Companies primarily argue that the orders were implemented in 1986 when 
such information was not readily available to the Authority or the public via the internet. 
Moton No. 14, p. 1; Motion No. 15, p. 1. Now, the Companies note that their SEC filings3 
are publicly available and easily accessible on their website, and that certain economic 
data components, such as inflation rates, are publicly available and no longer require a 
utility-specific filing. Motion No. 14, pp. 2-3; Motion No. 15, pp. 2-3. As such, the 
Companies assert that discontinuing the filing requirements set forth in Orders No. 1 and 
2 would promote administrative efficiency by eliminating unnecessary filings. Motion No. 
14, p. 1; Motion No. 15, p. 2. Finally, the Companies note that the Authority can request 

3 UI, CNG, SCG, and their parent company, Avangrid, are no longer publicly traded and no longer make 
filings with the SEC. Motion No. 14, p. 1. The Authority construes Motion No. 14 as a request to rescind 
Order 1 indefinitely, regardless of whether the companies were to become publicly traded in the future.

financial information from the Companies when circumstances warrant additional review. 
Motion No. 14, p. 1. 
OCC objects to the Companies’ request, arguing that it is not incumbent on 
Authority and OCC staff to search on the internet to obtain the required SEC filings and 
that the information provided in the filings are not a matter of record in any proceeding 
filed directly with the Authority OCC Objection, pp. 1-2. OCC further states that the 
information provided in Order Nos. 1 and 2 in this proceeding are important to 
understanding how the regulated utilities are performing in furtherance of OCC’s role in 
advocating for ratepayers. Id., p. 2. 
The Authority conducted a review and analysis of the docket history and intent, 
taking into consideration the perspectives of parties and the Authority’s statutory 
obligations and information needs. The Authority recognizes that Order Nos. 1 and 2 
have been in effect for 40 years and were enacted at a time when access to information 
such as SEC filings and economic data were not readily accessible via the internet. 
Conversely, the Authority recognizes that various stakeholders like OCC or Authority staff 
closely monitor certain data points in the filings and that a single point of access to such 
information via a docket filing can serve as an efficient method of accessing such 
information. Thus, the Authority attempts to balance administrative efficiency and the 
Companies’ respective filing burdens with maintaining ease of access for parties and 
Authority staff to particularly important information contained in Order Nos. 1 and 2. 
In striking this balance, the Authority determines that it is appropriate to rescind 
Order No. 1 as it pertains to the Companies given the broad accessibility of such filings 
on the internet. Moreover, the Authority alters Order No. 2 to remove the requirement 
that the Companies file items A, B, C, D, E, G, N, and O enumerated above because such 
information is either readily available at publicly accessible websites or is no longer 
effective at or essential for assessing the financial health or performance of the 
Companies. Furthermore, the information now being eliminated from the Companies’ 
compliance filings may be requested via discovery in a docketed proceeding or may 
otherwise be admitted into the evidentiary record pursuant to General Statutes § 4-178. 
The Companies shall continue to file items F, H, I, J, K, L, and M above and as set forth 
in Order No. 2 because they consist of the most important information needed to monitor 
the Companies’ respective financial performance and are still frequently accessed by 
OCC and Authority staff via this docket.
